Rep. Yakym’s bill highlights a critical flaw in Medicare’s bureaucracy: endless delays for life-saving tech. While streamlining approvals is a start, the real issue is systemic. H.R. 3069’s Medicare-for-All framework would amplify this dysfunction by centralizing control, not fixing it.

Cutting red tape is meaningless if D.C. still lets Big Pharma monopolize pricing and regulators drown innovation in compliance costs. True reform requires dismantling the entire graft cycle—where bureaucrats and corporations profit while patients wait.

This bill nibbles at the edges. Until Congress guts the FDA’s 10-year approval marathons and Medicare’s price-fixing schemes, seniors will keep losing.
